rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track;

SELECT ar.ArtistId, ar.Name, COUNT(al.AlbumId) AS AlbumCount FROM Artist ar JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name HAVING COUNT(al.AlbumId) = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM Album GROUP BY ArtistId))
rows.note: I'm counting albums per artist by ArtistId and returning all artists tied for the top count.

rows.sql: SELECT Country, COUNT(*) AS CustomerCount FROM Customer GROUP BY Country ORDER BY CustomerCount DESC, Country;
rows.note: Assuming "country" refers to the Customer table's Country column, and customers with a NULL country are grouped separately.

rows.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS Year, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS TotalRevenue FROM Invoice GROUP BY Year ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: Assumption: total revenue is the sum of Invoice.Total grouped by calendar year of InvoiceDate.

rows.sql: SELECT c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS FullName, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS TotalSpent FROM Customer c JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.FirstName, c.LastName ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC LIMIT 5
rows.note: Assumption: "total amount spent" is the sum of Invoice.Total per customer, and full name is FirstName plus LastName.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(c.CustomerId) AS CustomerCount FROM Customer c JOIN Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName, e.LastName HAVING COUNT(c.CustomerId) = (SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Customer WHERE SupportRepId IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SupportRepId))
rows.note: Assumption: "support rep" means Employee linked via Customer.SupportRepId, and I'll return all tied top reps.

I'm assuming "Grunge playlist" means the playlist named exactly "Grunge" (the only match for that name).

The Grunge playlist has **15 tracks**.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS tracks_never_purchased FROM Track WHERE TrackId NOT IN (SELECT TrackId FROM InvoiceLine WHERE TrackId IS NOT NULL);
rows.note: Assuming "never purchased" means the track does not appear in any InvoiceLine.

rows.sql: SELECT BillingCountry, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS Revenue FROM Invoice WHERE InvoiceDate >= '2012-01-01' AND InvoiceDate < '2013-01-01' GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assuming revenue means the sum of Invoice.Total grouped by BillingCountry for invoices dated in 2012, returning only the top country.

rows.sql: SELECT ar.Name FROM Artist ar JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId WHERE t.GenreId IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 3 ORDER BY ar.Name
rows.note: Assumption: a track's artist is reached via Track → Album → Artist, and I count distinct genres per artist.

rows.sql:
SELECT g.Name AS Genre,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) / (SELECT SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity) FROM InvoiceLine), 2) AS Percentage
FROM InvoiceLine il
JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
LEFT JOIN Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
GROUP BY g.GenreId, g.Name
ORDER BY Percentage DESC;
rows.note: I'll compute each genre's share of revenue from invoice lines (UnitPrice × Quantity), with tracks lacking a genre grouped under NULL.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT i.CustomerId) AS customer_count
FROM Invoice i
JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
WHERE g.Name = 'Rock'
  AND i.CustomerId NOT IN (
    SELECT i2.CustomerId
    FROM Invoice i2
    JOIN InvoiceLine il2 ON il2.InvoiceId = i2.InvoiceId
    JOIN Track t2 ON t2.TrackId = il2.TrackId
    JOIN Genre g2 ON g2.GenreId = t2.GenreId
    WHERE g2.Name = 'Jazz'
  );
rows.note: Assuming "bought" means the customer appears on an invoice containing a track whose genre is Rock (or Jazz).

rows.sql: SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS MonthNumber, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS Revenue FROM Invoice WHERE strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2011' GROUP BY MonthNumber ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I'll assume invoice revenue is the sum of `Invoice.Total` grouped by calendar month of `InvoiceDate` in 2011.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM Employee e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Customer c WHERE c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId)
rows.note: Assuming "assigned as support rep" means Customer.SupportRepId matches the employee's EmployeeId, and full name is FirstName plus LastName.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_first_purchase_2010 FROM (SELECT CustomerId, MIN(InvoiceDate) AS first_date FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId) WHERE first_date >= '2010-01-01' AND first_date < '2011-01-01'
rows.note: Assumption: a customer's first purchase is their earliest invoice date, and we count customers whose earliest invoice falls in 2010.

rows.sql: SELECT Album.Title, ROUND(SUM(Track.Milliseconds) / 60000.0, 1) AS Minutes FROM Track JOIN Album ON Track.AlbumId = Album.AlbumId GROUP BY Album.AlbumId, Album.Title ORDER BY SUM(Track.Milliseconds) DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I'll sum track milliseconds per album, then take the top album and convert to minutes.

rows.sql:
WITH y AS (
  SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS yr, SUM(Total) AS rev
  FROM Invoice GROUP BY yr
),
l AS (
  SELECT yr, rev, LAG(rev) OVER (ORDER BY yr) AS prev_rev FROM y
)
SELECT yr, ROUND(rev, 2) AS revenue,
       ROUND((rev - prev_rev) * 100.0 / prev_rev, 1) AS yoy_pct_change
FROM l
WHERE prev_rev IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY yr;
rows.note: I'm assuming revenue means the sum of `Invoice.Total` grouped by calendar year of `InvoiceDate`, and I'm excluding the first year since it has no prior year to compare against.

rows.sql: WITH cust AS (SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) AS spend FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId) SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_above_avg FROM cust WHERE spend > (SELECT AVG(spend) FROM cust);
rows.note: Assumption: "total spend" per customer is the sum of Invoice.Total across all their invoices, and the average is taken over customers who have invoices.

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT p.Name AS PlaylistName, COUNT(DISTINCT al.ArtistId) AS ArtistCount
  FROM Playlist p
  JOIN PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId
  JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = pt.TrackId
  JOIN Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
  GROUP BY p.PlaylistId, p.Name
)
SELECT PlaylistName, ArtistCount
FROM counts
WHERE ArtistCount = (SELECT MAX(ArtistCount) FROM counts);
SELECT COUNT(*) AS invoice_count FROM (SELECT il.InvoiceId FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId GROUP BY il.InvoiceId HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 1) AS x
rows.note: I'll count invoices whose line items map to more than one distinct genre through Track.GenreId.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS SupportRep, SUM(i.Total) AS Revenue2010 FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId JOIN Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId WHERE strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) = '2010' GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName, e.LastName ORDER BY Revenue2010 DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I'm assuming revenue is the sum of `Invoice.Total` for 2010 invoices, attributed to each customer's `SupportRepId`.

rows.sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) AS Year, g.Name AS Genre,
         SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS Revenue
  FROM InvoiceLine il
  JOIN Invoice i ON i.InvoiceId = il.InvoiceId
  JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
  JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
  GROUP BY Year, Genre
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT Year, Genre, Revenue,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY Year ORDER BY Revenue DESC) AS rnk
  FROM rev
)
SELECT Year, Genre, ROUND(Revenue, 2) AS Revenue
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk = 2
ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: Assumption: revenue is `UnitPrice * Quantity` per invoice line, grouped by the invoice's calendar year and the track's genre, with ties at second place all shown.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count
FROM (
  SELECT c.CustomerId,
         COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) = '2013' THEN i.Total END), 0) AS total_2013,
         COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) = '2012' THEN i.Total END), 0) AS total_2012
  FROM Customer c
  LEFT JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
  GROUP BY c.CustomerId
) t
WHERE total_2013 > total_2012;
rows.note: Assumption: spending is the sum of Invoice.Total by InvoiceDate year, and I count customers whose 2013 total is greater than their 2012 total (customers with no 2012 invoices count as 0).

rows.sql: SELECT AVG(Total) AS median_total FROM (SELECT Total FROM Invoice ORDER BY Total LIMIT 2 - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Invoice) % 2 OFFSET ((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Invoice) - 1) / 2)
rows.note: Assumption: median of the Total column across all rows in Invoice (for an even count, the average of the two middle values).

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT ar.ArtistId, ar.Name, COUNT(DISTINCT pt.PlaylistId) AS PlaylistCount
  FROM Artist ar
  JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
  JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
  JOIN PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.TrackId = t.TrackId
  GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name
)
SELECT ArtistId, Name, PlaylistCount
FROM counts
WHERE PlaylistCount = (SELECT MAX(PlaylistCount) FROM counts);
rows.note: I'm assuming an artist's tracks are linked through Album, and I'm counting distinct playlists that contain any of those tracks. Ties are included.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(1.0 * (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM InvoiceLine) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Invoice), 2) AS avg_line_items_per_invoice
rows.note: Assumption: line items are rows in InvoiceLine, and the average is taken over all invoices (including any with zero lines, if they exist).

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS discontinued_products FROM Products WHERE Discontinued = '1';
rows.note: Assuming Discontinued = '1' marks a discontinued product.

rows.sql: SELECT CompanyName FROM Suppliers WHERE Country = 'Germany';
rows.note: I'm assuming "based in Germany" means the Country column equals 'Germany'.

rows.sql: SELECT c.CategoryName, COUNT(p.ProductID) AS ProductCount FROM Categories c JOIN Products p ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName ORDER BY ProductCount DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT strftime('%Y', OrderDate) AS Year, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount FROM Orders GROUP BY Year ORDER BY Year;
SELECT s.CompanyName AS ShipperName, ROUND(AVG(o.Freight), 2) AS AvgFreight FROM Orders o JOIN Shippers s ON o.ShipVia = s.ShipperID GROUP BY s.ShipperID, s.CompanyName ORDER BY s.CompanyName;
rows.note: Assuming "shipper" means the ShipVia carrier on each order, I'll group Orders by the Shippers table and average Freight.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM Employees e WHERE e.ReportsTo = (SELECT EmployeeID FROM Employees WHERE FirstName = 'Andrew' AND LastName = 'Fuller')

WITH counts AS (
  SELECT e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2020'
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeID, FullName
)
SELECT FullName, OrderCount
FROM counts
WHERE OrderCount = (SELECT MAX(OrderCount) FROM counts);
SELECT COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM Products WHERE UnitPrice > (SELECT AVG(UnitPrice) FROM Products);
rows.note: Assuming "average product unit price" means the simple average of Products.UnitPrice across all products.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_shipped_to_france FROM Orders WHERE ShipCountry = 'France';
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped to France" means ShipCountry = 'France' in the Orders table, counting all orders regardless of whether ShippedDate is filled in.

rows.sql: SELECT p.ProductName, ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS Revenue FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.ProductName ORDER BY SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) DESC LIMIT 5
rows.note: Assuming revenue = UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from "Order Details", grouped by product name.

rows.sql: SELECT c.CategoryName, p.ProductName, p.UnitPrice FROM Products p JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID WHERE p.UnitPrice = (SELECT MAX(p2.UnitPrice) FROM Products p2 WHERE p2.CategoryID = p.CategoryID) ORDER BY c.CategoryName
rows.note: I'll assume "most expensive" means the highest UnitPrice in Products within each category, with ties all included.

rows.sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT o.CustomerID, SUM(d.UnitPrice * d.Quantity * (1 - d.Discount)) AS Revenue
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" d ON d.OrderID = o.OrderID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2021'
  GROUP BY o.CustomerID
)
SELECT c.CompanyName, r.Revenue
FROM rev r
JOIN Customers c ON c.CustomerID = r.CustomerID
WHERE r.Revenue = (SELECT MAX(Revenue) FROM rev)
rows.note: I'm assuming revenue means the sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) over order lines, grouped by customer, using orders dated in 2021.

rows.sql:
WITH m AS (
  SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS month, COUNT(*) AS n
  FROM Orders
  WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2021'
  GROUP BY month
)
SELECT month, n FROM m WHERE n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM m);
rows.note: I'm counting orders by `OrderDate` in calendar year 2021 and returning every month tied for the highest count.
The database contains no orders from 1997. The Orders table's OrderDate values range from 2012-07-10 to 2023-10-28, so no employee can be credited with orders in 1997.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS late_shipped_orders FROM Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL AND ShippedDate > RequiredDate
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped after their required date" means ShippedDate is not NULL and ShippedDate > RequiredDate.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(ShippedDate) - julianday(OrderDate)), 1) AS avg_days_to_ship FROM Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL;
rows.note: Assuming "shipped orders" means orders with a non-NULL ShippedDate, and days are computed as the difference of julian day values (fractional days averaged, then rounded).

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM Products WHERE Discontinued = '0' AND UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel;
rows.note: Assuming "still sold" means Discontinued = '0' and "below reorder level" means UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel.

rows.sql: SELECT c.Country, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount FROM Orders o JOIN Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2019-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2020-01-01' GROUP BY c.Country ORDER BY OrderCount DESC LIMIT 1;

SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c.CategoryName = 'Beverages' THEN od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) / SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 1) AS beverages_pct FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2023-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2024-01-01';
rows.note: I'll compute revenue as UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) for orders dated in 2023, and take the Beverages share of the total.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_with_orders_every_month_2020 FROM (SELECT CustomerID FROM Orders WHERE OrderDate >= '2020-01-01' AND OrderDate < '2021-01-01' GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%m', OrderDate)) = 12);
rows.note: I'm counting customers who have orders in all 12 calendar months of 2020, based on `OrderDate`.

rows.sql:
WITH ov AS (
  SELECT o.EmployeeID, o.OrderID, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS val
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID
),
avg_e AS (
  SELECT EmployeeID, AVG(val) AS avg_val FROM ov GROUP BY EmployeeID
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS full_name, a.avg_val
FROM avg_e a
JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = a.EmployeeID
WHERE a.avg_val = (SELECT MAX(avg_val) FROM avg_e);
rows.note: I'm treating each order's value as the sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) over its lines, and averaging those values per employee.

rows.sql: SELECT s.CompanyName, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS Revenue FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID JOIN Suppliers s ON s.SupplierID = p.SupplierID WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2018' GROUP BY s.SupplierID, s.CompanyName ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assumption: revenue = UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from Order Details, filtered to orders dated in 2018.

rows.sql:
WITH s AS (
  SELECT od.ProductID,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2021' THEN od.Quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units_2021,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2022' THEN od.Quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units_2022
  FROM "Order Details" od
  JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
  GROUP BY od.ProductID
),
r AS (
  SELECT p.ProductName, s.units_2021, s.units_2022, (s.units_2022 - s.units_2021) AS increase
  FROM s JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = s.ProductID
)
SELECT * FROM r WHERE increase = (SELECT MAX(increase) FROM r);
rows.note: I'm assuming "units sold" means the sum of `Quantity` in Order Details, grouped by the year of `OrderDate`, and that the increase is 2022 minus 2021.

rows.sql:
SELECT s.CompanyName AS ShipperName,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN o.ShippedDate > o.RequiredDate THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS LatePercentage
FROM Orders o
JOIN Shippers s ON s.ShipperID = o.ShipVia
WHERE o.ShippedDate IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY s.ShipperID, s.CompanyName
ORDER BY s.CompanyName;
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped orders" means orders with a non-NULL ShippedDate, and "arrived after the required date" means ShippedDate > RequiredDate.

rows.sql: SELECT year, order_count, SUM(order_count) OVER (ORDER BY year ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_count FROM (SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS year, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders GROUP BY year) ORDER BY year
rows.note: Assumption: count orders per calendar year from OrderDate, then accumulate in year order.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM (SELECT OrderID, SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) AS total FROM "Order Details" GROUP BY OrderID HAVING total > 10000);
rows.note: I'm assuming each order's total is the sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) over its line items, excluding freight.

rows.sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT o.EmployeeID,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2018' THEN od."UnitPrice" * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) AS rev2018,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2019' THEN od."UnitPrice" * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) AS rev2019
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  GROUP BY o.EmployeeID
),
diff AS (
  SELECT EmployeeID, rev2018, rev2019, rev2019 - rev2018 AS growth FROM rev
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS employee_name, d.rev2018, d.rev2019, d.growth
FROM diff d
JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = d.EmployeeID
WHERE d.growth = (SELECT MAX(growth) FROM diff)
rows.note: I'm assuming revenue is SUM(UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount)) over order lines, grouped by the order's year, with the full name as FirstName plus LastName.
